instruction: Start only after task 0009-efile-diligence completes successfully. Read IRS_EFILE_DILIGENCE.md and IRS_EFILE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and implement the maximum production-quality e-file foundation that can lawfully be built before Folio receives any required IRS/state approvals. Follow the recommended architecture from the diligence rather than assuming a direct-transmitter path. Build a provider-neutral e-file domain model and workflow covering return package/version, taxpayer/client ownership, preparer/firm EFIN metadata without storing unnecessary secrets, form-family support matrix, tax year, submission readiness, signature authorization, validation results, packaging status, transmission status, acknowledgements, reject codes, correction/resubmission history, state coupling, and immutable audit events. Build schema/business-rule ingestion/versioning mechanisms for authorized IRS packages, XML generation/validation boundaries, deterministic preflight validation, canonical acknowledgement/reject parsing, idempotent submission orchestration, retry rules limited to transient transport failures, and an explicit ATS adapter separate from production. Implement a transmitter interface that can support either Folio's eventual MeF transmitter or an authorized third-party transmitter without changing the user-facing workflow. Add an E-file Center UI with returns by stage, ready-to-file queue, signatures missing, validation failures, transmitted/accepted/rejected statuses, reject explanations, deadlines, state linkage, drill-down to source evidence, and clear professional approval before submission. No production transmission endpoint may become active without explicit configuration proving the required authorization/certification identifiers are present; fail closed otherwise. Do not fabricate IRS credentials, software IDs, ETINs, EFINs, certificates, or approvals. Do not send real returns. Add comprehensive unit/integration tests using fixtures and ATS-safe mocks, including tenant isolation, signature gating, validation gating, duplicate submission prevention, acknowledgement idempotency, reject/resubmit transitions, state coupling, and authorization fail-closed behavior. Run full tests, typecheck, production build, Wrangler dry-run, Rust/Windows checks where affected. Commit and push to main. Do not deploy production.
